real_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to close-up dogs (and similar furry animals) that face the camera or the left, fill much of the frame, and are cut off by its edges. It responds least to subjects facing right. Part of the preference for frontal, close, frame-filling subjects is shared with similar units. What is particular to this unit is the left-versus-right facing asymmetry and the preference for subjects cropped by the frame edge.

real_s2.explanation: A dog-face/close-up unit. It is most active when a large dog (or dog's head) fills much of the frame, is cropped by the photo edges, and faces the camera or to the left. It is notably weak for subjects facing right, which is the most distinctive trait relative to similar units. It also prefers frames without visible straight lines or horizons, i.e. tight crops on fur and face rather than scenes. Small, distant or absent main subjects reduce its response.

real_s3.explanation: This unit responds to close, frontal views of dogs (and similar furry animals) that fill much of the frame and run off its edges. It is weakest when the animal faces right, small, or when there is no single subject. What sets it apart from its similar units is a left-right asymmetry: it fires clearly more for subjects facing left than facing right. It also prefers subjects cut off by the photo border, with little visible horizon or straight lines.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to dogs and other furry, dog-like animals, chiefly breeds with long or fluffy coats and small terriers. Within those classes it is somewhat more active when the animal faces or points left, compared with facing right or facing the camera. It is also more active when the animal is small in the frame, and somewhat more active when the animal is off-centre to the right. The left-facing preference is the most distinctive signal, but the similar units only partly share it.

null_s2.explanation: This unit responds to dogs and other furry carnivores. Beyond the class, it favors subjects facing or pointing left over those facing right or toward the camera. It also leans weakly toward small subjects placed in the right third of the frame and toward slightly blurry subjects. Its preference for small subjects is shared with similar units, so it is not particular to this unit.

null_s3.explanation: A dog-selective unit (mostly small and medium breeds, plus weasel) that prefers animals facing or pointing left. Its activity is higher when the subject faces left than when it faces right or toward the camera. It also leans toward small subjects that take up little of the frame, and toward subjects in the right third. The left-facing preference is the part most particular to this unit, since its similar units sit near the middle of the distribution on those rows. Small-subject effects rest on only 5 photos and the similar units are also high there, so they are less distinctive.
